subject: SOC 2 Finding: Investigation Results, Temporary Controls & Next Steps
messages:
From: Lisa Tang <lisa.tang@verityaudit.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SOC 2 control test - user access review exception (Finera scope)

Hi Priya (and Diego),

During our interim testing for Finera's SOC 2 Type II period we observed an exception in the monthly access review control for the RedEdge application scoped to Finera. Specifically: two accounts with privileged group membership were not included in the May review export; the control evidence shows the export generation step skipped a secondary group filter.

Can you confirm whether this was an isolated export configuration issue or indicative of a broader change in the export pipeline? We flagged the finding as a control exception and will need management's response and remediation evidence for our report.

Requested items:
- Root cause assessment describing why the two accounts were missed (high level is fine).
- Interim/temporary compensating controls in place while remediation is underway.
- Expected remediation ETA and evidence plan (screenshots, logs, or updated playbook).

Appreciate a response by end of day Thursday (May 20) so we can align language for the audit report.

Thanks,
Lisa Tang
Senior Auditor, Verity Audit
lisa.tang@verityaudit.com

--
Attachment: test_export_sample.csv (referenced in body)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Tang <lisa.tang@verityaudit.com>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 11:03:22 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC 2 control test - user access review exception (Finera scope)

Hi Lisa —

Thank you for the clear note and timeline. We’ve opened an investigation and I’ve asked Diego to provide a technical root cause and an interim control plan. High-level summary from a first pass: it appears the export job that generates the monthly access review CSV used an old filter param after a recent deployment to the export service (a safe-guard param name changed: `include_secondary_groups -> include_extra_groups`). That mismatch resulted in missing rows for accounts only present in the secondary group set.

Actions we are taking immediately:
- Temporary compensating control: manual export and cross-check of privileged groups for Finera until the export job is patched (daily cadence, owner: Security Ops).
- Creation of an automated alert if export row count changes by >5% compared to the prior cycle (owner: Platform Reliability).
- Diego will provide a remediation ETA and artifact list by tomorrow EOD.

I’m attaching a short note with our initial findings and the temporary controls matrix. We can also provide proposed bridge language for Finera if you need wording for the auditor report.

If you need anything more formal for the file, let me know and I’ll escalate to Marcus for signature.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Director, Compliance & Trust
Redwood Inference

Attachments: soc2_finding_root_cause_notes.pdf; temporary_controls_matrix.xlsx

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Lisa Tang <lisa.tang@verityaudit.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 08:45:10 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC 2 control test - user access review exception (Finera scope)

Folks —

Technical root cause (concise):
- During the 2027-05-05 deploy of export-service v2.3.1 we refactored the filter parameter names to make them more generic. A subset of release tests missed verifying the migration shim for the legacy scheduled-export job used by Finera’s instance. As a result, the scheduled job invoked the old param name and the downstream selector returned an empty set for secondary-group-only members.

Remediation plan and ETA:
- Fix: restore backward-compatible shim and add explicit param mapping in the scheduled-export job. PR will be submitted today. Patch ETA: 24 hours.
- Hardening: add unit test that exercises the export param mapping plus an integration smoke test in the scheduled job. ETA: 5 business days to merge and verify into production.
- Evidence pack: PR link, CI run logs, smoke test output, pre/post-export CSV diff for the May and June cycles. We will also provide a screenshot of the alert rule being added to PagerDuty and a signed temporary control attestation from Security Ops.

Interim controls (in flight):
1) Daily manual export & reconciliation (Security Ops) — owner assigned, checklist created.
2) Temporary read-only freeze on changes to export config for Finera scope until smoke tests are complete.
3) PagerDuty alert for export row count delta (>5%) — currently in staging, will be live within 12 hours.

I’ve uploaded the detailed root cause notes and a temporary controls matrix to the Finera evidence folder. Attaching the remediation timeline figure for visibility.

Diego
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: remediation_timeline_gantt.png

Subject: RE: SOC 2 control test - user access review exception (Finera scope)

Lisa / Finera team —

Appreciate the patience while we validated the cause. Per Diego’s investigation and the steps below, Redwood is providing the following deliverables for the SOC 2 interim file and for Finera’s records:

Deliverables (to be available in the evidence folder by EOD May 21):
- Root cause summary (pdf) — describes the parameter mismatch and scope of affected accounts.
- Patch PR and CI logs (links) — demonstrates the fix and successful CI runs.
- Pre/post export CSV diff for May exports and a validated June export (CSV) showing the reconciled rows.
- Temporary controls matrix (xlsx) — owner sign-offs and daily checklist logs.
- Screenshot of the PagerDuty alert rule and confirmation it is live.
- Management response memo with suggested bridge language for the audit report.

Temporary controls are in effect and owned by Security Ops; we expect the production patch to land within 24 hours and the integration verification to complete within five business days. If Verity requires a signed bridge letter or a short management statement for Finera, we can prepare that and route for Marcus’ signature.

Please confirm whether the deliverables above meet your needs for the auditor file or if you would prefer a one-page management response tailored specifically to Verity's wording. If Finera would like direct wording to include in customer communications, we can provide proposed copy.

Thanks — we’ll circulate the evidence links as soon as the artifacts are uploaded.

Regards,
Priya Natarajan
Director, Compliance & Trust
Redwood Inference
